entries.description: The AAV Assault Amphibious Vehicle is primarily used by the United States Marine Corps (USMC) rather than the Army. AAVs are also commonly called "Amtracs," which is short for "amphibious tractors." The AAV-7A1 is the current model in use and has been in service since the early 1970s. It is designed to transport troops from ships to shore and vice versa, as well as provide support during ground operations.

It is not merely an extension of the traditional Abrams tank lineage, but rather a fresh concept, designed to tackle emerging threats on the contemporary battlefield.

entries.description: The Amphibious Combat Vehicle – 30 mm Cannon (ACV-30) is the medium-caliber fire-support variant of the U.S. Marine Corps Amphibious Combat Vehicle family. Developed by BAE Systems and Iveco Defence Vehicles as an engineering change to the ACV-P, the vehicle retains the common 8×8 ACV powertrain, drivetrain, amphibious propulsion, communications, navigation and survivability architecture while incorporating a modified upper hull and a Kongsberg RT20 remotely operated turret.

Hull, Crew Arrangement and Survivability: The ACV-30 retains the common ACV 8×8 armored hull while incorporating a modified upper structure to accommodate the Kongsberg RT20 turret, ammunition-handling equipment, and associated electronics. It preserves the ACV-P’s core powertrain, drivetrain, water-propulsion system, navigation and communications architecture, and survivability features, maintaining a high degree of commonality across th

The gun is distinguished by its high muzzle velocity and thermal sleeve. While early versions lacked thermal imaging, upgrades like the AMX-30B2 included modernized fire control with laser rangefinders and passive night vision systems. Production commenced in 1993 with the first production vehicles completed at the Alvis Vickers Leeds facility in 1994. The Challenger 2 MBT was accepted in service with the British Army in 1994. entries.description: The Cobra is a 4x4 armored personnel carrier (APC) designed and manufactured by Streit Group. It is based on the Toyota Land Cruiser 200 series and features a combination of ballistic steel monocoque body, mild steel inner floor, and under-body blast protection. This APC can be utilized by modern armed forces in diverse battlefield scenarios, as well as by law enforcement agencies when agility and protection are crucial.

Cougar is an ideal APC that handles well on rough terrains and facilitates the users with ultimate maneuverability on and off-road.

entries.description: The M1 is the first variant of the US Abrams series main battle tank, developed from 1971 to answer a US Army request. The Chrysler Corporation prototype was selected in November 1976 to enter Full-Scale Engineering Development. Total production of the M1 was 2,374 tanks, the last delivered in February 1985. The M1 is no longer in service with the US military, most having been upgraded to M1A1 and M1A2 standard.
